newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end down on eve of listing flood.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end down on eve of listing flood.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices closed lower on Wednesday on selling triggered by concerns that the forthcoming listing of a number of new issues would suck funds away from existing shares, brokers said.
The B share index dipped 2.41 points or 1.64 percent to 144.53 on turnover of HK$77 million, compared with Tuesday's HK$51 million.
The domestic A share index slipped 0.38 points or 0.08 percent to 463.21 on turnover of 9.2 billion yuan against 10.0 billion yuan on Tuesday.
"People cut their positions ahead of a flood of new listings and a long holiday," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
Seven companies will float a combined 340 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, a record in the number of daily new company listings on the south China bourse, brokers said.
In addition, three companies will go public in the city's A share market on Friday.
In term of B shares, China's giant Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd has completed its initial public offering (IPO) of 460 million B shares for listing in Shenzhen in early July.
Bengang raised about one billion yuan from the IPO.
The Shenzhen bourse has announced it would close on June 30 and July 1 to mark Britain's handover Hong Kong to China and trading will resume on Wednesday July 2.

Today's falls in the city's A and B share markets were also linked to concerns that Beijing may carry out some new anti-speculation measures in July, after the British colony reverts to Beijing's rule at midnight on June 30, brokers said.
They also said B shares fell sharply on growing short-term pessimism among investors in light of the market's recent prevailing bearishness.
"The B share market's recent poor performance dampened investor confidence," the China Guotai analyst said.
"I am not optimistic about the B share market's performance late this week," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Jiangling Motors was the biggest loser on the B share market, tumbling HK$0.27 or 7.83 percent to HK$3.18.

Television tube maker SEG Co, which registered heavy losses in the past two sessions, rebounded HK$0.45 or 6.43 percent to HK$7.45 to be the second best performer. Volume hit 4.0 million shares, making it the most actively traded B share.
On the A share market, recently-listed First Automobile edged down 0.03 yuan to 14.58 yuan on massive volume of 137 million shares. It was the most actively traded A share.
